newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan land auction price 40 pct higher than base.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan land auction price 40 pct higher than base.

text.p: Taiwan's finance ministry said it auctioned a large piece of state land on Monday in Taipei's commercial district at a winning bid price 40 percent higher than the base price due to drastic competition.
The bidding for the 42,552 square-foot parcel was participated in by eight bidders. Unlisted Nan Shan Life Insurance Co won with a price of T$2.72 billion, a ministry official told Reuters.
The bidding marked the first time in 10 years that the ministry had auctioned a piece of state land larger than 36,000 square feet, the official said.
"We are quite satisfied with the result," the official said.
The ministry completed auctioning for nine of 21 pieces of state land it opened for bids, he said.
Analysts said the result boded well for the expected gradual recovery of the domestic real estate market.

"Although this land is for commercial use, not for residential usage, the drastic competition still shows the property prices are bottoming out and in a gradual recovery," said Nomura Securities analyst Amy Huang.

Taiwan's real estate market has been in a slump since peaking in 1989. But recent strong economic indicators and rising land sales indicated that the market may have begun a gradual recovery, analysts said.
